note: Judged 2026-11-27 independently against RFC 5216 Section 5.3 (rfc/full/rfc5216.txt): "When performing this comparison, implementations MUST follow the validation rules specified in Section 3.1 of [RFC2818]." Verified producing code (identity.go::verifyServerCertificate/serverIdentityMatches/matchSingleLabelWildcard/mostSpecificCommonName, peer.go::startTLSClient, peer_chain.go::verifyConnection) and all 4 tagged tests in rfc5216_identity_test.go. Positive (TestRFC5216ServerIdentityRFC2818Rules): exact ASCII case-insensitive DNS SAN, leftmost single-label wildcard *.example.com, exact IPv4/IPv6 against iPAddress SAN, exact NAI against rfc822Name SAN, and most-specific (last) Subject CN fallback only when no SAN extension exists. Negative (TestRFC5216ServerIdentityRFC2818Rules, TestRFC5216IdentityIsTakenFromTheSANAndAuthorized, TestRFC5216ResumedSessionReverifiesPeerAndServerIdentity, TestRFC5216FailClosedWhenIdentityPolicyUnset): refuses mismatched SAN despite matching CN, multi-label and apex matches against *.example.com, single-label *.com and partial/inner wildcards (v*.example.com, a.*.example.com), IP literal against dNSName or CN, CN when any SAN extension exists (even IP-only), earlier non-most-specific CN, ClientAuth-only EKU on server cert, updated ServerIdentity on a resumed TLS 1.3 session, and empty/wildcard ServerIdentity at startTLSClient. Cleanly isolated across all cases.
